decoding="async" width="200" height="125" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/de/Population_Density_by_Pakistani_District_-_2017_Census.svg/300px-Population_Density_by_Pakistani_District_-_2017_Census.svg.png 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/de/Population_Density_by_Pakistani_District_-_2017_Census.svg/400px-Population_Density_by_Pakistani_District_-_2017_Census.svg.png 2x" data-file-width="3200" data-file-height="2000" /></a></span></div><div class="thumbcaption text-align-center">Population Density per square kilometre of each Pakistani District as of the 2017 Pakistan Census</div></div></div><div class="trow"><div class="tsingle" style="width:202px;max-width:202px"><div class="thumbimage"><span typeof="mw:File"><a href="/wiki/File:Population_by_Pakistani_District_-_2017_Census.svg" class="mw-file-description"><img alt="" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/bc/Population_by_Pakistani_District_-_2017_Census.svg/200px-Population_by_Pakistani_District_-_2017_Census.svg.png" decoding="async" width="200" height="125" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/bc/Population_by_Pakistani_District_-_2017_Census.svg/300px-Population_by_Pakistani_District_-_2017_Census.svg.png 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/bc/Population_by_Pakistani_District_-_2017_Census.svg/400px-Population_by_Pakistani_District_-_2017_Census.svg.png 2x" data-file-width="3200" data-file-height="2000" /></a></span></div><div class="thumbcaption text-align-center">Population of each Pakistani District as of the 2017 Pakistan Census</div></div></div></div></div>
<div class="excerpt-block"><style data-mw-deduplicate="TemplateStyles:r1066933788">.mw-parser-output .excerpt-hat .mw-editsection-like{font-style:normal}</style><link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable dablink excerpt-hat selfref">This section is an excerpt from <a href="/wiki/Demographics_of_Pakistan" title="Demographics of Pakistan">Demographics of Pakistan</a>.<span class="mw-editsection-like plainlinks"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a class="external text" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Demographics_of_Pakistan&amp;action=edit">edit</a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div><div class="excerpt">
<p>Pakistan had a population of 241,492,197 or 241.49 Million according to the final results of the <a href="/wiki/2023_Census_of_Pakistan" class="mw-redirect" title="2023 Census of Pakistan">2023 Census</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-Demographics_of_Pakistan_2017CensusPopulation_450-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Demographics_of_Pakistan_2017CensusPopulation-450">&#91;446&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-Demographics_of_Pakistan_AJKPop_451-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Demographics_of_Pakistan_AJKPop-451">&#91;447&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-Demographics_of_Pakistan_GBPop_452-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Demographics_of_Pakistan_GBPop-452">&#91;448&#93;</a></sup> This figure includes Pakistan's <a href="/wiki/Provinces_of_Pakistan" class="mw-redirect" title="Provinces of Pakistan">four provinces</a> e.g. Punjab, Sindh, KPK, Balochistan and <a href="/wiki/Islamabad_Capital_Territory" title="Islamabad Capital Territory">Islamabad Capital Territory</a> . AJK and Gilgit-Baltistan's census data is yet to be approved by CCI Council of Pakistan. Pakistan is the world's <a href="/wiki/List_of_countries_by_population" class="mw-redirect" title="List of countries by population">fifth most populous country</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-Demographics_of_Pakistan_UNWPP2019_453-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Demographics_of_Pakistan_UNWPP2019-453">&#91;449&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>Between 1951 and 2017, Pakistan's population expanded over sixfold, going from 33.7&#160;million to 207.7&#160;million. The country has a relatively high, although declining, growth rate supported by high birth rates and low death rates. Between 1998 and 2017, the average annual population growth rate stood at +2.40%.
</p><p>Dramatic social changes have led to urbanisation and the emergence of two <a href="/wiki/Megacity" title="Megacity">megacities</a>: <a href="/wiki/Karachi" title="Karachi">Karachi</a> and <a href="/wiki/Lahore" title="Lahore">Lahore</a>. The country's urban population more than tripled between 1981 and 2017 (from 23.8&#160;million to 75.7&#160;million), as Pakistan's <a href="/wiki/Urbanisation_rate" class="mw-redirect" title="Urbanisation rate">urbanisation rate</a> rose from 28.2% to 36.4%. Even with this, the nation's urbanisation rate remains one of <a href="/wiki/Urbanization_by_country" class="mw-redirect" title="Urbanization by country">the lowest in the world</a>, and in 2017, over 130 million Pakistanis (making up nearly 65% of the population) lived in <a href="/wiki/Rural_area" title="Rural area">rural areas</a>.
</p><p>Due to a high <a href="/wiki/Total_fertility_rate" title="Total fertility rate">fertility rate</a>, estimated at 3.5 in 2022, Pakistan has one of the world's <a href="/wiki/List_of_countries_by_median_age" title="List of countries by median age">youngest populations</a>. The 2017 census recorded that 40.3% of the country's population was under the age of 15, while only 3.7% of Pakistanis were aged 65 or more.<sup id="cite_ref-Demographics_of_Pakistan_2017CensusAge_454-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Demographics_of_Pakistan_2017CensusAge-454">&#91;450&#93;</a></sup> The <a href="/wiki/Median_age" class="mw-redirect" title="Median age">median age</a> of the country was 19,<sup id="cite_ref-Demographics_of_Pakistan_2017CensusAge_454-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Demographics_of_Pakistan_2017CensusAge-454">&#91;450&#93;</a></sup> while its <a href="/wiki/Sex_ratio" title="Sex ratio">sex ratio</a> was recorded to be 105 males per 100 females.<sup id="cite_ref-Demographics_of_Pakistan_2017CensusPopulation_450-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Demographics_of_Pakistan_2017CensusPopulation-450">&#91;446&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
The <a href="/wiki/Demographic_history_of_Pakistan" title="Demographic history of Pakistan">demographic history of Pakistan</a> from the ancient <a href="/wiki/Indus_Valley_civilisation" class="mw-redirect" title="Indus Valley civilisation">Indus Valley civilisation</a> to the modern era includes the arrival and settlement of many cultures and ethnic groups in the modern region of Pakistan from <a href="/wiki/Eurasia" title="Eurasia">Eurasia</a> and the nearby <a href="/wiki/Middle_East" title="Middle East">Middle East</a>. Because of this, Pakistan has a multicultural, multilinguistic, and multiethnic society. Despite <a href="/wiki/Urdu" title="Urdu">Urdu</a> being Pakistan's <a href="/wiki/Lingua_franca" title="Lingua franca">lingua franca</a>, estimates on how many languages are spoken in the country range from 75 to 85,<sup id="cite_ref-455" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-455">&#91;451&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-Demographics_of_Pakistan_GlottologPK_456-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Demographics_of_Pakistan_GlottologPK-456">&#91;452&#93;</a></sup> and in 2017, the country's three largest <a href="/wiki/Ethnolinguistic_group" title="Ethnolinguistic group">ethnolinguistic groups</a> were the <a href="/wiki/Punjabis" title="Punjabis">Punjabis</a> (making up 38.8% of the total population), the <a href="/wiki/Pashtuns" title="Pashtuns">Pashtuns</a> (18.2%), and the <a href="/wiki/Sindhis" title="Sindhis">Sindhis</a> (14.6%).<sup id="cite_ref-Demographics_of_Pakistan_2017CensusLanguage_457-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Demographics_of_Pakistan_2017CensusLanguage-457">&#91;453&#93;</a></sup> Pakistan is also thought to have the world's fourth-largest <a href="/wiki/List_of_countries_by_refugee_population" title="List of countries by refugee population">refugee population</a>, estimated at 1.4&#160;million in mid-2021 by the <a href="/wiki/United_Nations_High_Commissioner_for_Refugees" title="United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees">UNHCR</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-Demographics_of_Pakistan_RefugeesUNHCR_458-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Demographics_of_Pakistan_RefugeesUNHCR-458">&#91;454&#93;</a></sup></div></div>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Ethnicity_and_languages">Ethnicity and languages</span></h3>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main articles: <a href="/wiki/Languages_of_Pakistan" title="Languages of Pakistan">Languages of Pakistan</a> and <a href="/wiki/Ethnic_groups_in_Pakistan" class="mw-redirect" title="Ethnic groups in Pakistan">Ethnic groups in Pakistan</a></div>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">See also: <a href="/wiki/Pakistanis" title="Pakistanis">Pakistanis</a></div>
<figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Mother_Tongue_by_Pakistani_District_-_2017_Census.svg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/a8/Mother_Tongue_by_Pakistani_District_-_2017_Census.svg/220px-Mother_Tongue_by_Pakistani_District_-_2017_Census.svg.png" decoding="async" width="220" height="138" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/a8/Mother_Tongue_by_Pakistani_District_-_2017_Census.svg/330px-Mother_Tongue_by_Pakistani_District_-_2017_Census.svg.png 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/a8/Mother_Tongue_by_Pakistani_District_-_2017_Census.svg/440px-Mother_Tongue_by_Pakistani_District_-_2017_Census.svg.png 2x" data-file-width="3200" data-file-height="2000" /></a><figcaption><div style="text-align: center">Dominant Ethnolinguistic Group in each Pakistani <a href="/wiki/Districts_of_Pakistan" title="Districts of Pakistan">District</a> as of the <a href="/wiki/2017_Pakistan_Census" class="mw-redirect" title="2017 Pakistan Census">2017 Pakistan Census</a><sup id="cite_ref-2017CensusLanguage_6-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-2017CensusLanguage-6">&#91;6&#93;</a></sup></div></figcaption></figure>
<p>Pakistan is a multicultural, multi-linguistic, and multiethnic society. Despite <a href="/wiki/Urdu" title="Urdu">Urdu</a> being Pakistan's <a href="/wiki/Lingua_franca" title="Lingua franca">lingua franca</a>, estimates on how many languages are spoken in the country range from 75 to 85,<sup id="cite_ref-459" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-459">&#91;455&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-GlottologPK_460-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-GlottologPK-460">&#91;456&#93;</a></sup> Urdu—the <i>lingua franca</i> and a symbol of <a href="/wiki/Muslim_nationalism_in_South_Asia" title="Muslim nationalism in South Asia">Muslim identity</a> and national unity—is the national language and understood by over 75% of Pakistanis. It is the main medium of communication in the country, but the primary language of only 7% of the population.<sup id="cite_ref-2017_Census_461-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-2017_Census-461">&#91;457&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-462" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-462">&#91;458&#93;</a></sup> Urdu and English are the <a href="/wiki/Official_language" title="Official language">official languages</a> of Pakistan. English is primarily used in official business and government, and in legal contracts;<sup id="cite_ref-ciafactbook_161-6" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-ciafactbook-161">&#91;157&#93;</a></sup> the local variety is known as <a href="/wiki/Pakistani_English" title="Pakistani English">Pakistani English</a>. The enforcement of Urdu to the exclusion of other majority languages has been criticised; in particular, the expulsion of Pashto from the institutional domains and deprivation of state patronage has been shown to create conditions in which Pashtuns are placed at social, cultural, and economic disadvantage.<sup id="cite_ref-463" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-463">&#91;459&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>According to the <a href="/wiki/2017_Census_of_Pakistan" class="mw-redirect" title="2017 Census of Pakistan">2017 national census of Pakistan</a>, the country's largest <a href="/wiki/Ethnolinguistic_group" title="Ethnolinguistic group">ethnolinguistic groups</a> were the <a href="/wiki/Punjabis" title="Punjabis">Punjabis</a> (making up 38.8% of the total population), the <a href="/wiki/Pashtuns" title="Pashtuns">Pashtuns</a> (18.2%), <a href="/wiki/Sindhis" title="Sindhis">Sindhis</a> (14.6%), <a href="/wiki/Saraiki_people" title="Saraiki people">Saraikis</a> (12.19%), <a href="/wiki/Muhajir_(Pakistan)" title="Muhajir (Pakistan)">Muhajirs</a> (7.08%), and the <a href="/wiki/Baloch_people" title="Baloch people">Balochs</a> (3.02%).<sup id="cite_ref-2017CensusLanguage_6-2" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-2017CensusLanguage-6">&#91;6&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-464" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-464">&#91;460&#93;</a></sup> The remaining population consist of a number of ethnic minorities such as the <a href="/wiki/Brahui_people" title="Brahui people">Brahuis</a>,<sup id="cite_ref-:14_465-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:14-465">&#91;461&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-466" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-466">&#91;462&#93;</a></sup> the <a href="/wiki/Hindkowans" title="Hindkowans">Hindkowans</a>, the various peoples of Gilgit-Baltistan, the Kashmiris, the <a href="/wiki/Siddi" title="Siddi">Sheedis</a> (who are of African descent),<sup id="cite_ref-467" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-467">&#91;463&#93;</a></sup> and the <a href="/wiki/Hazara_people" class="mw-redirect" title="Hazara people">Hazaras</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-468" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-468">&#91;464&#93;</a></sup> There are also scattered speakers of <a href="/wiki/Gujarati_language" title="Gujarati language">Gujarati</a> in Karachi.<sup id="cite_ref-469" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-469">&#91;465&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>There is also a large <a href="/wiki/Pakistani_diaspora" title="Pakistani diaspora">Pakistani diaspora</a> worldwide, numbering over seven million,<sup id="cite_ref-470" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-470">&#91;466&#93;</a></sup> which has been recorded as the sixth largest diaspora in the world.<sup id="cite_ref-:3_471-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:3-471">&#91;467&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Immigration">Immigration</span></h3>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main article: <a href="/wiki/Immigration_to_Pakistan" title="Immigration to Pakistan">Immigration to Pakistan</a></div>
<figure class="mw-default-size mw-halign-left" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Tarbela_Dam_Area.JPG" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/d8/Tarbela_Dam_Area.JPG/220px-Tarbela_Dam_Area.JPG" decoding="async" width="220" height="165" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/d8/Tarbela_Dam_Area.JPG/330px-Tarbela_Dam_Area.JPG 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/d8/Tarbela_Dam_Area.JPG/440px-Tarbela_Dam_Area.JPG 2x" data-file-width="1600" data-file-height="1200" /></a><figcaption>Pakistan hosts the second largest refugee population globally after Turkey.<sup id="cite_ref-472" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-472">&#91;468&#93;</a></sup> An Afghan refugee girl near <a href="/wiki/Tarbela_Dam" title="Tarbela Dam">Tarbela Dam</a>.</figcaption></figure>
<p>Even after partition in 1947, Indian Muslims continued to migrate to Pakistan throughout the 1950s and 1960s, and these migrants settled mainly in Karachi and other towns of Sindh province.<sup id="cite_ref-473" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-473">&#91;469&#93;</a></sup> The wars in neighboring Afghanistan during the 1980s and 1990s also forced millions of <a href="/wiki/Afghan_refugees" title="Afghan refugees">Afghan refugees</a> into Pakistan. The <a href="/wiki/Census_in_Pakistan" title="Census in Pakistan">Pakistan census</a> excludes the 1.41&#160;million registered <a href="/wiki/Afghans_in_Pakistan" title="Afghans in Pakistan">refugees from Afghanistan</a>,<sup id="cite_ref-474" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-474">&#91;470&#93;</a></sup> who are found mainly in the <a href="/wiki/Khyber_Pakhtunkhwa" title="Khyber Pakhtunkhwa">Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa</a> and <a href="/wiki/Federally_Administered_Tribal_Areas" title="Federally Administered Tribal Areas">tribal belt</a>, with small numbers residing in <a href="/wiki/Karachi" title="Karachi">Karachi</a> and <a href="/wiki/Quetta" title="Quetta">Quetta</a>. Pakistan is home to one of the world's largest <a href="/wiki/Refugee" title="Refugee">refugee</a> populations.<sup id="cite_ref-475" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-475">&#91;471&#93;</a></sup> In addition to Afghans, around 2&#160;million <a href="/wiki/Bangladeshis_in_Pakistan" class="mw-redirect" title="Bangladeshis in Pakistan">Bangladeshis</a> and half a million other undocumented people live in Pakistan. They are claimed to be from other areas such as <a href="/wiki/Myanmar" title="Myanmar">Myanmar</a>, Iran, Iraq, and Africa.<sup id="cite_ref-476" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-476">&#91;472&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>Experts say that the migration of both Bengalis and Burmese (<a href="/wiki/Rohingya_people" title="Rohingya people">Rohingya</a>) to Pakistan started in the 1980s and continued until 1998. Shaikh Muhammad Feroze, the chairman of the Pakistani Bengali Action Committee, claims that there are 200 settlements of Bengali-speaking people in Pakistan, of which 132 are in Karachi. They are also found in various other areas of Pakistan such as Thatta, Badin, Hyderabad, Tando Adam, and Lahore.<sup id="cite_ref-477" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-477">&#91;473&#93;</a></sup> Large-scale Rohingya migration to Karachi made that city one of the largest population centres of Rohingyas in the world after Myanmar.<sup id="cite_ref-478" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-478">&#91;474&#93;</a></sup> The Burmese community of Karachi is spread out over 60 of the city's slums such as the Burmi Colony in Korangi, Arakanabad, Machchar colony, Bilal colony, Ziaul Haq Colony, and Godhra Camp.<sup id="cite_ref-479" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-479">&#91;475&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>Thousands of <a href="/wiki/Uyghurs" title="Uyghurs">Uyghur</a> Muslims have also migrated to the Gilgit-Baltistan region of Pakistan, fleeing religious and cultural persecution in Xinjiang, China.<sup id="cite_ref-480" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-480">&#91;476&#93;</a></sup> Since 1989 thousands of <a href="/wiki/Kashmiris" title="Kashmiris">Kashmiri</a> Muslim refugees have sought refuge in Pakistan, complaining that many of the refugee women had been raped by Indian soldiers and that they were forced out of their homes by the soldiers.<sup id="cite_ref-481" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-481">&#91;477&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Urbanisation">Urbanisation</span></h3>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main article: <a href="/wiki/Urbanisation_in_Pakistan" title="Urbanisation in Pakistan">Urbanisation in Pakistan</a></div>
<figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Kalma_Underpass1.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/4a/Kalma_Underpass1.jpg/220px-Kalma_Underpass1.jpg" decoding="async" width="220" height="146" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/4a/Kalma_Underpass1.jpg/330px-Kalma_Underpass1.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/4a/Kalma_Underpass1.jpg/440px-Kalma_Underpass1.jpg 2x" data-file-width="679" data-file-height="450" /></a><figcaption><a href="/wiki/Kalma_Underpass" title="Kalma Underpass">Kalma Underpass</a>, <a href="/wiki/Lahore" title="Lahore">Lahore</a></figcaption></figure>
<p>Since <a href="/wiki/Independence_of_Pakistan" class="mw-redirect" title="Independence of Pakistan">achieving independence</a> as a result of the <a href="/wiki/Partition_of_India" title="Partition of India">partition of India</a>, the <a href="/wiki/Urbanisation_in_Pakistan" title="Urbanisation in Pakistan">urbanisation</a> has increased exponentially, with several different causes. The majority of the population in the south resides along the Indus River, with <a href="/wiki/Karachi" title="Karachi">Karachi</a> the most populous commercial city.<sup id="cite_ref-The_Urban_Frontier—Karachi_482-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-The_Urban_Frontier—Karachi-482">&#91;478&#93;</a></sup> In the east, west, and north, most of the population lives in an arc formed by the cities of <a href="/wiki/Lahore" title="Lahore">Lahore</a>, <a href="/wiki/Faisalabad" title="Faisalabad">Faisalabad</a>, <a href="/wiki/Rawalpindi" title="Rawalpindi">Rawalpindi</a>, <a href="/wiki/Islamabad" title="Islamabad">Islamabad</a>, <a href="/wiki/Sargodha" title="Sargodha">Sargodha</a>, <a href="/wiki/Gujranwala" title="Gujranwala">Gujranwala</a>, <a href="/wiki/Sialkot" title="Sialkot">Sialkot</a>, <a href="/wiki/Gujrat_city" class="mw-redirect" title="Gujrat city">Gujrat</a>, <a href="/wiki/Jhelum" title="Jhelum">Jhelum</a>, <a href="/wiki/Sheikhupura" title="Sheikhupura">Sheikhupura</a>, <a href="/wiki/Nowshera,_Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa" class="mw-redirect" title="Nowshera, Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa">Nowshera</a>, <a href="/wiki/Mardan" title="Mardan">Mardan</a>, and <a href="/wiki/Peshawar" title="Peshawar">Peshawar</a>. During the period 1990–2008, city dwellers made up 36% of Pakistan's population, making it the most urbanised nation in South Asia. Furthermore, more than 50% of Pakistanis live in towns of 5,000 people or more.<sup id="cite_ref-Jason_Burke_483-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Jason_Burke-483">&#91;479&#93;</a></sup> <a href="/wiki/Immigration_to_Pakistan" title="Immigration to Pakistan">Immigration</a>, from both within and outside the country, is regarded as one of the main factors contributing to urbanisation in Pakistan. One analysis of the <a href="/wiki/1998_Pakistan_Census" class="mw-redirect" title="1998 Pakistan Census">1998 national census</a> highlighted the significance of the <a href="/wiki/Partition_of_India" title="Partition of India">partition of India</a> in the 1940s as it relates to urban change in Pakistan.<sup id="cite_ref-Clark_484-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Clark-484">&#91;480&#93;</a></sup>
During and after the independence period, <a href="/wiki/Muhajir_(Urdu-speaking_people)" class="mw-redirect" title="Muhajir (Urdu-speaking people)">Urdu speaking Muslims</a> from India migrated in large numbers to Pakistan, especially to the port city of <a href="/wiki/Karachi" title="Karachi">Karachi</a>, which is today the largest metropolis in Pakistan. <a href="/wiki/Immigration_to_Pakistan" title="Immigration to Pakistan">Migration from other countries</a>, mainly from those nearby, has further accelerated the process of urbanisation in Pakistani cities. Inevitably, the rapid urbanisation caused by these large population movements has also created new political and socio-economic challenges. In addition to immigration, economic trends such as the green revolution and political developments, among a host of other factors, are also important causes of urbanisation.<sup id="cite_ref-Clark_484-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Clark-484">&#91;480&#93;</a></sup>
</p>

<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Religion">Religion</span></h3>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main article: <a href="/wiki/Religion_in_Pakistan" title="Religion in Pakistan">Religion in Pakistan</a></div>
<div class="barbox tright" style="overflow-x: auto;">
<div style="border:1px solid silver; font-size:88%; padding:0.4em; width:auto; background: white;">
